title: Somites: blocks that keep time

objective.text: Explain how somites form and how they are used to date an embryo.

body.general: How old is a week-4 embryo? Count its somites, paired blocks of tissue along the back [f5]. They come from paraxial mesoderm, the middle-layer strip beside the midline [f1,f2]. In the head it stays as loose, unsegmented whorls called somitomeres, which become loose head tissue [f1,f2]. The first pair appears near the future back of the skull at about day 20 [f3]. About three new pairs are added each day, toward the tail [f4]. Each block later helps build the backbone, ribs and back muscles [f10]. In month 2, head-to-bottom length is used instead [f6].
body.mbbs: Paraxial mesoderm first forms whorl-like somitomeres, starting at the head end [f1]. In the head they stay unsegmented and give head mesenchyme; from the occipital region down they become somites [f2]. The first pair appears in the occipital region at about day 20 [f3]. New pairs follow craniocaudally at about three pairs a day [f4]. This steady pace lets the somite count date the embryo in weeks 3–4 [f5]. In month 2, crown–rump length takes over [f6]. There are 4 occipital and 8 cervical pairs [f7]. Langman gives 42–44 pairs by the end of week 5, with 12 thoracic, 5 lumbar, 5 sacral and 8–10 coccygeal [f8]. The first occipital and the last 5–7 coccygeal pairs later disappear [f9]. Each somite then divides into parts for vertebrae, ribs, muscle and dermis [f10].

facts.text: Paraxial mesoderm first forms whorl-like somitomeres, starting at the head end.
In the head the somitomeres stay unsegmented and give head mesenchyme; from the occipital region down they become somites.
The first pair of somites appears in the occipital region at about day 20.
New pairs follow in head-to-tail order at about three pairs a day.
Because somites appear so regularly, their count dates the embryo in weeks 3–4.
In month 2, crown–rump length replaces the somite count for dating.
There are 4 occipital and 8 cervical somite pairs.
The book gives 42–44 somite pairs by the end of week 5: 4 occipital, 8 cervical, 12 thoracic, 5 lumbar, 5 sacral and 8–10 coccygeal.
The book has the first occipital pair and the last 5–7 coccygeal pairs disappearing later.
Each somite later divides into parts that build vertebrae, ribs, back and body-wall muscles, and dermis.
⚑ Newer evidence (D-039): human serial-section counts find at most 38–39 somite pairs, at stages 14–16.
Beyond Langman: in human stem-cell models the segmentation clock ticks about every 5 hours. This is in a dish, not the embryo's somite rate.

misconceptions.wrong: Somites are segments of the neural tube.
misconceptions.right: Somites are blocks of paraxial mesoderm lying beside the neural tube (future spinal cord).

misconceptions.wrong: Loose head tissue (head mesenchyme) comes from somites.
misconceptions.right: In the head, paraxial mesoderm stays as unsegmented somitomeres; somites start at the back of the skull (occipital region).

misconceptions.wrong: Somite count dates the embryo through the whole embryonic period.
misconceptions.right: It works only in weeks 3–4; in month 2 we use crown–rump length (head-to-bottom length).

options: Blocks of paraxial mesoderm beside the neural tube (future spinal cord)
Folds of ectoderm along the back
checks.why: Somites bud from paraxial mesoderm and lie beside the neural tube (future spinal cord); they are not part of it.

checks.prompt: An embryo has about 10 pairs of somites. About how old is it?
checks.why: The first pair appears about day 20 and about three pairs are added a day, so 10 pairs is about day 22–23.

checks.prompt: When does counting somites stop being the way to date an embryo?
checks.why: Somite counts date weeks 3–4; in month 2 crown–rump length (head-to-bottom length) is used.

adult: Each somite goes on to help build vertebrae, ribs, back and body-wall muscles, and dermis (deep skin) [f10].

remember.q: Where and when does the first somite pair appear?
remember.a: Near the future back of the skull (occipital region), at about day 20 [f3].

remember.q: How fast are new somite pairs added?
remember.a: About three pairs a day, from head to tail [f4].

remember.q: How many somite pairs does Langman give in total?
remember.a: 42–44 pairs by the end of week 5 [f8].

remember.q: What does paraxial mesoderm form in the head?
remember.a: Unsegmented somitomeres that become loose head tissue (head mesenchyme), not somites [f2].
